overview: Two major regions of the brain, with very different jobs — higher thought and voluntary control versus balance and coordination.
genZNote: Cerebrum: the thinking, deciding, personality headquarters. Cerebellum: the balance and coordination backstage crew.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Controls higher functions: thinking, memory, voluntary movement, sensory perception, personality.
aspects.valueB: Coordinates balance, posture, and fine-tunes voluntary muscle movements.

aspects.label: Relative Size
aspects.valueA: The largest part of the human brain.
aspects.valueB: Smaller, located below and behind the cerebrum.

aspects.label: Effect of Damage
aspects.valueA: Can affect memory, speech, personality, or specific sensory/motor functions depending on location.
aspects.valueB: Typically causes loss of coordination and balance (ataxia), without affecting intelligence directly.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Cerebellar damage classically produces ataxia (a loss of coordinated movement) while leaving conscious thought and decision-making intact.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cerebrum = the big thinker. Cerebellum = the 'little brain' fine-tuning movement and balance.
overlay.commonMisconception: The cerebellum does not initiate voluntary movement — it only coordinates and fine-tunes movements that are initiated by the cerebrum's motor cortex.
